Inure

/in-YOOR/ - rhymes with secure · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Inure means to make someone accustomed to something unpleasant.

Two seasons of subway commutes had inured Malik to shoulder-to-shoulder crowds.

Worked Example

Guides on the high tea route are inured to the thin air that leaves their clients gasping at every switchback; four years of carrying loads up the pass will do it.

Inure is habituation to something unpleasant, and it keeps its preposition: inured to the cold, to criticism, to noise. Being inured is not numbness — the hardship is still felt, just bearable — and pleasant routines don't qualify: nobody is inured to Saturday pancakes.

How Inure Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

harden

harden: to toughen generally — no repeated exposure required

toughen

toughen: to build resistance, physical or mental

accustom

accustom: to make familiar with anything, pleasant or not

Antonyms

coddle

coddle: to shelter from every discomfort

sensitize

sensitize: to make more responsive to it, not less

How Strong Is It? — familiarize → inure → numb

familiarize vs. inure

familiarize vs. inure: To familiarize just makes something known — it stops short of inure, which toughens you against something genuinely unpleasant.

numb vs. inure

numb vs. inure: Numb goes further than inure: the inured worker still feels the hardship and bears it, while the numbed one has stopped feeling it at all.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of inure.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: in (the English preposition, not the negative prefix)

Root — -ure

Root — -ure: use, work, practice (obsolete English ure)

Put it together

Put it together: No Latin prefix at all: inure grew out of the Middle English phrase in ure — 'in use, in practice.' Ure, an old noun for work or use, survives nowhere else; what stays 'in use' long enough becomes bearable, and the phrase fused into a verb. The in- is the plain English preposition wearing a disguise.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Inure hides no prefix and no Latin root: it is the old phrase 'in ure' — in use, in practice — welded into one word. Ure itself, a medieval noun for work or use, has vanished from English entirely, so there is no cousin left to compare.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal

Inure is the formal verb for exposure doing its slow work, always to something unpleasant: hardship, noise, criticism. Accustom covers pleasant and neutral routines; numb means the feeling itself has died. If the thing is nice, you have simply gotten used to it.
